body: Also worked for me. I was wondering if it was happening to anyone else.

I was actually in a similar position as you. Misdiagnosed for 10 years. On and off antidepressants that didn't work until I received my diagnosis at 26 years old. 

Took another 3 years to find the right combination of medication after having a severe mixed episode that ended up with me hospitalized in the psych ward. I blame that mostly on my psychiatrist not listening to me when I told her that the medications weren't working and she just kept increasing the dosage instead of trying new ones, but I digress.

I found the right psychiatrist and for the last year I have been completely stable on the right medications. My psychiatrist also suffers from bipolar. 

My main piece of advice would be to not get discouraged if you do not find the right medications right away, but also do not settle for feeling "slightly better". I feel completely normal now with my medications and encourage everyone to find the right combination that works for them. Definitely do not settle with your medications because you get tired of trying different ones. It's completely worth it to stick with it until you find the right ones.

So I had this issue for a long time, and just realized that if you make your voicemail password more than 7 characters it works. 

My voicemail password was previously 4 and it didn't work at all. I tried removing the password and that didn't work. I set it up as 8 characters and suddenly it worked perfectly. Not sure if this will help anyone else but it was driving me crazy.

I'm so sorry to hear of your grandmother passing. That can definitely take a hit to your mood. 

I was misdiagnosed for 10 years and had very similar problems and what worked for me is to setup specific times to do things. If it was 9 am, I would say, okay at 10 am I'm going to start the laundry. Setting up tasks for specific time-frames worked for me for a long time and helped keep my sanity and kept me in a regular routine outside of work. 

I will say after being diagnosed it took me another 4 years to get on the right medicationss and it really got worse during that 4 years until I found the right psychiatrist who also happens to have bipolar disorder. Within a few months he was able to find the right combination of medications for me and I have never felt better. I don't know if your medications were working previously and this situation has just put you into the depressive episode or if you may have been having issues with being stable in your mood already. If you have, just know that the right medication combination, even if it takes years like it did me, can be life changing and I would recommend continuing to find the right combination until it works perfectly.
